applied: explain.text: "A transformer needs AC" is too broad: pulse and switch-mode transformers run on chopped DC, which still changes; and on DC the supply and leads limit the current too, not only the winding. Narrowed to a changing current and to the coil itself.

practice.text: "Only its winding's resistance would limit the current" is not true of a real DC feed: the supply's own resistance, its leads and any current limit also act. Narrowed to what the coil itself offers.

interactive.whatAmILookingAt: "A quarter cycle ahead" depends on sign convention: with Lenz's minus sign, textbook phasor diagrams put the induced emf a quarter cycle behind the flux. Reworded to the convention-free fact that the emf peaks as the flux crosses zero.

interactive.ignores: It says the core is drawn as never saturating, yet DC mode marks the flux bar Saturated; the two disagree. Narrowed to Hand and AC, with DC's saturation named as drawn only by the bar.

analogy.breaks: "A car's speed does nothing to stop it moving" is false in everyday life: air drag grows with speed and slows the car. Narrowed to the speedometer's reading, which truly pushes back on nothing.
